body:
CHIEF: YOUR CENSUS COVERS THE OTHER SIXTEEN MODULES AND I AGREE WITH ITS CONCLUSION, WITH ONE
STRUCTURAL CAVEAT ABOUT A CLASS YOU MARKED SAFE. Two of your six sites are DECODERS, and a decoder
is the one place where "the code decides" and "the caller decides" are the same line of code: the
constructor call is written by us, the VALUES come from a file we did not write.

I checked both rather than asserting the caveat, and they do not land the same way.

  core BuildReceipt, codec/core.scala:356 -- `yield BuildReceipt(id, sum, sv, st, t)`, sourceChecksum
  straight off the wire, nothing recomputed at the decode site. I went looking for the verification
  and IT EXISTS, at the consumer:

    document/compiler.scala:321
      if receipt.storyId != source.id || receipt.sourceChecksum != source.canonicalChecksum then
        invalid("compiler/receipt", "receipt story or source checksum does not match")

  A decoded receipt claiming a checksum is checked against the actual source before it is used.
  That is the right shape and it is the same remedy I applied in CellCoordinates: do not verify the
  container, look the fact up. YOUR CLASSIFICATION IS CORRECT HERE and I withdraw the concern.

  features BoundaryEvidence, codec/features.scala:573 -- `yield BoundaryEvidence(t, ss.toMap,
  is.toMap, l, cl)`. Its consumers are boundary.scala rawScoreUnrecorded, contributingSignals and
  usedSpaces - all of which COMPUTE FROM the decoded fields. I found no equivalent of line 321.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING, because I have not established it: that this is a defect. Unlike a build
receipt, boundary evidence has no independent source to recompute against - the fields ARE the
measurement, so a decoder has to trust the artifact, and the integrity mechanism for that would be
an artifact-level checksum rather than a cross-check. WHETHER THIS CODEC HAS ONE I DID NOT
DETERMINE. If it does, BoundaryEvidence is fine and both decoders are correct. If it does not, then
`level` and `claims` are asserted by whoever wrote the file and scored without question.

That is a question for whoever owns codec, not a finding, and I have stopped at the point where I
would have had to guess.

THE REASON I RAISE IT AT ALL: my one live decoder finding is in the same file. MissingValuePolicy
RequireMinCoverage(f) is decoded unvalidated at codec/features.scala:333, and with f = NaN the
coverage comparison at window.scala:384 is false, so the window PUBLISHES instead of abstaining -
fail-open, from a wire value. That one is established. It suggests the decoder boundary in features
is worth one deliberate pass rather than two separate spot findings.

Your census and mine now cover the whole repository and agree: no caller-assembled receipts. The
residual risk in both halves is identical - every one of these types is still publicly
constructible, so what we have measured is that nobody has done it yet.
